promise: Make the task easier to complete, and show what evidence would prove the change helped.
audience: Teams designing or reviewing digital workflows and human-agent experiences.
trigger: Use when task completion, cognitive load, accessibility, authority, error recovery, or longitudinal impact needs investigation.

modes.name: Frame and gather
modes.when: The product surface is known but the actual breakdown is unclear.
modes.output: A task model, claim-level evidence map, and ranked uncertainties.

modes.name: Review and recommend
modes.output: Mechanism-specific findings, authority choices, and observable acceptance criteria.

modes.name: Verify
modes.when: A decision package needs an adversarial check or study.
modes.output: A bounded verdict, valid study plan, and explicit inference limits.

examples.title: A recovery button is not recovery evidence
examples.brief: A fictional analyst cannot recover a failed batch without re-entering every field.
examples.before: Add an animated retry button and call the workflow accessible and faster.
examples.after: Walk the failure state, preserve user input, expose what retry will do, provide cancellation, and define a keyboard and task-completion check before claiming improvement.
examples.why: Visual polish can support the task, but it cannot establish usability or conformance.

boundaries: Expert inspection is not observed-user evidence; anecdotes cannot establish prevalence.
Accessibility conformance needs adequate runtime/manual evidence at the stated scope.
Visual Taste guidance is an optional craft lens; it never outranks task evidence, usability, or user voice.

marketing.headline: Make the next step easier to understand and do.
marketing.lead: An evidence-led UX skill for workflows and human-agent interactions. Trace the real task, find where people can lose their way and turn findings into changes you can verify.

benefits.title: Find the task behind the screen
benefits.body: Map decisions, interruptions, errors, recovery and completion instead of beginning with a visual redesign.

benefits.title: Make authority understandable
benefits.body: Show who decides, who acts, what can be stopped and what evidence confirms completion.

benefits.title: Give recommendations a fair test
benefits.body: Separate observation from inference and specify what would pass or fail each consequential change.

walkthrough.title: Frame and inspect
walkthrough.detail: Name the actor and task, gather relevant evidence and walk both normal and failure states.

walkthrough.title: Recommend a concrete change
walkthrough.detail: Choose the lenses that fit: cognition, accessibility, authority, recovery and visual craft.

walkthrough.title: Verify at the right level
walkthrough.detail: Check keyboard and runtime behavior, then use affected-user tasks where the claim needs them.

use_when: People cannot tell what happened or what to do next.
A workflow loses input or hides recovery after an error.
An agent interface makes approval, cancellation or completion unclear.
not_for: An accessibility-conformance certificate based on a source scan.
Treating anecdotes as prevalence or a visual preference as measured usability.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use UX Ergonomics to review this fictional batch-import failure flow. The analyst loses entered mappings after an error. Separate observation, inference and recommendation; propose recovery behavior and keyboard/task checks without claiming a measured improvement.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional finding: failed import discards mappings
Observation: inputs disappear after the error
Consequence: task must restart from scratch
Change: preserve mappings; explain retry and cancellation
Acceptance: keyboard user can inspect and retry without re-entry
Evidence gap: affected-user task observation pending
marketing.proof_summary: Native bundle structure, references and portable installation are checked. No usability study or accessibility-conformance claim is established by those structural checks; each product needs validation on its actual tasks and surfaces.
marketing.next_step: Bring one user task, an inspectable flow and the breakdown you want to understand.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.

name: amplifier-capability-ux-ergonomics
version_basis: No project version recorded; version remains null. The shared portable installer selects source with an explicit full Git commit; legacy and native routes follow their own documentation.

portable_method.name: ux-ergonomics
portable_method.contract: Agent Skills directory; caller applies the method; no independent execution loop is installed.

portable.input: Caller task and explicitly authorized context
portable.output: Make the task easier to complete, and show what evidence would prove the change helped.
portable.failure: Report insufficient evidence, unsupported context or host limitation; never turn discovery into an execution claim.

native.status: Existing declared entrypoints preserved; runtime signatures, service access and installation tests remain separate evidence.

installation.scope: Shared canonical portable installer only; not the legacy repository helper or native package installation.

runtime.status: Host/caller authorizes each operation; installation is not a tool allowlist or standing approval.
declared_boundaries: Expert inspection is not observed-user evidence; anecdotes cannot establish prevalence.

secret_names.native_runtime_inventory: See native documentation; no credentials are bundled or inferred.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: Forty fields. Then it's gone.
film.blurb: In 68 seconds, Pat maps forty columns and loses them all to one failed import. UX Ergonomics rides the real route to the stop where it breaks, keeps the work, says what retry will do, gives a way out and checks it with only a keyboard. It will not call the fix better until real people try it. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: Pat, the import and the form are a fictional example. The film shows how the skill behaves; it does not report results.
